name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_RESPIRATION_IN_PLANTS_MCQ_Q01 - Gaseous exchange adaptations in terrestrial plants

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding gaseous exchange and respiration in plants:

(A) Plants possess specialized respiratory organs like lungs and gills for rapid gaseous exchange.
(B) Each plant part takes care of its own gas-exchange needs with very little transport of gases between organs.
(C) Roots, stems, and leaves respire at rates significantly lower than those observed in animals.
(D) In thick woody stems, living cells are confined to thin layers inside and beneath the bark, while the interior cells are dead.
(E) The loose packing of parenchyma cells in leaves, stems, and roots provides an interconnected system of air spaces.

Which of the following options contains only the correct statements?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of statement (A)
Plants lack specialized respiratory organs such as lungs or gills; instead, diffusion through stomata and lenticels accounts for all gaseous exchange. Thus, this statement is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of statement (B)
Each plant part caters to its individual gas-exchange needs, and there is negligible translocation of respiratory gases from one part to another. Thus, this statement is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of statement (C)
Plants have relatively low metabolic demands compared to animals, so their organs respire at substantially lower rates. Thus, this statement is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of statement (D)
In bulky woody stems and roots, living tissues are organized in thin peripheral sheets beneath the bark with lenticels, whereas the central bulk comprises non-living mechanical tissues. Thus, this statement is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of statement (E)
Parenchymatous cells in various plant tissues are loosely packed, creating an extensive interconnected network of intercellular spaces facilitating gas diffusion. Thus, this statement is correct.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Statements (B), (C), (D), and (E) are correct, while statement (A) is incorrect. Hence, the correct combination is (B), (C), (D), and (E) only.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_RESPIRATION_IN_PLANTS_MCQ_Q02 - Enzymatic reactions and intermediates of glycolysis

questiontext.text:
Read the following five statements concerning the glycolytic pathway (EMP pathway):

(A) Hexokinase catalyses the irreversible phosphorylation of glucose to glucose-6-phosphate with the consumption of ATP.
(B) Sucrose is cleaved into glucose and fructose by the enzyme amylase prior to entering glycolysis.
(C) Invertase catalyses the conversion of fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate.
(D) Generation of \(\text{NADH} + \text{H}^+\) occurs during the oxidation of glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate to 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate.
(E) Substrate-level phosphorylation directly yields ATP during the conversion of phosphoenolpyruvate to pyruvic acid.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of statement (A)
The priming reaction of glycolysis involves hexokinase, which phosphorylates glucose to glucose-6-phosphate using one molecule of ATP. Thus, this statement is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of statement (B)
In plants, sucrose is broken down into glucose and fructose by invertase (sucrase), not amylase. Thus, this statement is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of statement (C)
The phosphorylation of fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate is catalyzed by phosphofructokinase, not invertase. Thus, this statement is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of statement (D)
The oxidation of glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (PGAL) coupled with inorganic phosphate yields 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate (BPGA), during which \(\text{NAD}^+\) is reduced to \(\text{NADH} + \text{H}^+\). Thus, this statement is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of statement (E)
The dephosphorylation of phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) to pyruvate transfers a high-energy phosphate group to ADP, generating ATP by substrate-level phosphorylation via pyruvate kinase. Thus, this statement is correct.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Only statements (A), (D), and (E) are correct, whereas statements (B) and (C) are incorrect. Hence, the correct combination is (A), (D), and (E) only.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_RESPIRATION_IN_PLANTS_MCQ_Q03 - Features of anaerobic fermentation versus aerobic respiration

questiontext.text:
Assess the validity of the following five statements regarding fermentation:

(A) In lactic acid fermentation, pyruvic acid is directly reduced to lactic acid without any decarboxylation.
(B) Alcohol fermentation by yeast involves both decarboxylation and reduction steps.
(C) Less than seven percent of the total energy contained in glucose is released during fermentation.
(D) Reoxidation of \(\text{NADH} + \text{H}^+\) to \(\text{NAD}^+\) proceeds very vigorously in fermentation compared to aerobic respiration.
(E) Yeasts poison themselves to death when the accumulated ethanol concentration reaches approximately 13 percent.

Identify the option containing only correct statements:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of statement (A)
Lactate dehydrogenase reduces pyruvic acid directly into lactic acid using \(\text{NADH} + \text{H}^+\); no \(\text{CO}_2\) is released. Thus, this statement is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of statement (B)
In yeast fermentation, pyruvic acid first undergoes decarboxylation via pyruvic acid decarboxylase to form acetaldehyde and \(\text{CO}_2\), followed by reduction via alcohol dehydrogenase to ethanol. Thus, this statement is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of statement (C)
In anaerobic fermentation, less than \(7\%\) of the chemical energy stored in glucose is extracted and conserved into ATP. Thus, this statement is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of statement (D)
The oxidation of \(\text{NADH}\) to \(\text{NAD}^+\) is slow and incomplete in fermentation, whereas it is very vigorous and rapid in aerobic respiration via the electron transport chain. Thus, this statement is incorrect.

Step 5: Evaluation of statement (E)
Yeast cells suffer ethanol toxicity and cease metabolic activity when the ethanol concentration in their medium reaches roughly \(13\%\). Thus, this statement is correct.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Statements (A), (B), (C), and (E) are correct, while statement (D) is incorrect. Hence, the correct combination is (A), (B), (C), and (E) only.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_RESPIRATION_IN_PLANTS_MCQ_Q04 - Decarboxylation and phosphorylation in TCA cycle

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding the Tricarboxylic Acid (TCA) cycle:

(A) Citrate synthase catalyses the initial condensation of the acetyl group with oxaloacetic acid and water to produce citric acid.
(B) A five-carbon intermediate, \(\alpha\)-ketoglutaric acid, is produced as a result of oxidative decarboxylation of isocitrate.
(C) During the conversion of succinyl-CoA to succinic acid, a molecule of GTP is formed via substrate-level phosphorylation.
(D) In one turn of the TCA cycle starting from acetyl CoA, there are two points where \(\text{FAD}^+\) is reduced to \(\text{FADH}_2\).
(E) The conversion of succinyl-CoA to \(\alpha\)-ketoglutaric acid involves the synthesis of ATP directly from ADP.

Choose the option that includes all the true statements:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of statement (A)
The TCA cycle initiates with the condensation of acetyl CoA (\(2\text{C}\)) with oxaloacetic acid (\(4\text{C}\)) and \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\), driven by citrate synthase to yield citric acid (\(6\text{C}\)) and free CoA. Thus, this statement is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of statement (B)
Isocitrate (\(6\text{C}\)) undergoes oxidative decarboxylation, releasing \(\text{CO}_2\) and generating \(\text{NADH} + \text{H}^+\) to form the five-carbon intermediate \(\alpha\)-ketoglutaric acid. Thus, this statement is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of statement (C)
The cleavage of the thioester bond in succinyl-CoA to produce succinic acid is coupled to the substrate-level phosphorylation of GDP to GTP (which subsequently converts ADP to ATP). Thus, this statement is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of statement (D)
In each turn of the TCA cycle, there is only one step where \(\text{FAD}^+\) is reduced to \(\text{FADH}_2\) (during succinate oxidation to fumarate), whereas \(\text{NAD}^+\) is reduced at three distinct points. Thus, this statement is incorrect.

Step 5: Evaluation of statement (E)
The sequence proceeds from \(\alpha\)-ketoglutaric acid to succinyl-CoA, and then succinyl-CoA to succinate; it does not run in reverse, nor does conversion from succinyl-CoA form \(\alpha\)-ketoglutaric acid. Thus, this statement is incorrect.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Statements (A), (B), and (C) are correct, whereas statements (D) and (E) are incorrect. Hence, the correct combination is (A), (B), and (C) only.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_RESPIRATION_IN_PLANTS_MCQ_Q05 - Complexes and chemiosmosis in the mitochondrial ETS

questiontext.text:
Analyze the following five statements concerning the mitochondrial Electron Transport System (ETS) and oxidative phosphorylation:

(A) Ubiquinone receives reducing equivalents via Complex I (\(\text{NADH}\) dehydrogenase) and Complex II (succinate dehydrogenase).
(B) Cytochrome c is a mobile electron carrier attached to the inner surface facing the matrix of the inner mitochondrial membrane.
(C) Complex IV possesses cytochromes \(a\) and \(a_3\), along with two copper centres.
(D) Molecular oxygen serves as the terminal electron acceptor and is reduced to water.
(E) Passage of \(4\text{H}^+\) from the intermembrane space into the matrix through the \(F_0\) channel couples to the synthesis of one ATP molecule.

Which statement combination consists strictly of correct statements?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of statement (A)
Ubiquinone (located within the inner mitochondrial membrane) collects electrons from Complex I via \(\text{NADH}\) oxidation and from Complex II via \(\text{FADH}_2\) oxidation. Thus, this statement is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of statement (B)
Cytochrome c is a small peripheral protein attached to the outer surface of the inner membrane (facing the intermembrane space), acting as a shuttle between Complex III and IV, not facing the matrix. Thus, this statement is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of statement (C)
Complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase) contains cytochrome \(a\), cytochrome \(a_3\), and two distinct copper centres (\(\text{Cu}_A\) and \(\text{Cu}_B\)). Thus, this statement is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of statement (D)
Oxygen acts as the terminal electron and proton acceptor, driving electron flow through the chain and generating water molecules. Thus, this statement is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of statement (E)
According to the chemiosmotic coupling mechanism described in the textbook, the translocation of \(4\text{H}^+\) down the electrochemical gradient from the intermembrane space to the matrix through the \(F_0\) channel synthesizes one molecule of ATP at the \(F_1\) headpiece. Thus, this statement is correct.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Statements (A), (C), (D), and (E) are correct, while statement (B) is incorrect. Hence, the correct combination is (A), (C), (D), and (E) only.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_RESPIRATION_IN_PLANTS_MCQ_Q06 - Amphibolic pathways and respiratory quotient determinations

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following five statements concerning amphibolic pathways and respiratory quotient (RQ):

(A) Glycerol enters the respiratory breakdown pathway after being transformed into 3-phosphoglyceraldehyde (PGAL).
(B) Fatty acids must be degraded to acetyl CoA before they can enter the respiratory pathway.
(C) The respiratory pathway is considered purely catabolic because respiration only mediates destructive breakdown of substrates.
(D) When tripalmitin is completely oxidized as a respiratory substrate, the calculated RQ value is approximately 0.7.
(E) Pure proteins or pure fats are normally used as the primary respiratory substrates in living cells.

Which of the following options represents all the true statements?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of statement (A)
Fats are hydrolyzed into glycerol and fatty acids. Glycerol is phosphorylated and converted to dihydroxyacetone phosphate or PGAL (3-phosphoglyceraldehyde) to enter glycolysis. Thus, this statement is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of statement (B)
Fatty acids undergo beta-oxidation to form two-carbon acetyl CoA units, which then enter the TCA cycle. Thus, this statement is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of statement (C)
The respiratory pathway involves both catabolic breakdown and anabolic synthesis (e.g., acetyl CoA is withdrawn for fatty acid synthesis, oxaloacetate and \(\alpha\)-ketoglutarate for amino acid synthesis). Hence, it is an amphibolic pathway, not purely catabolic. Thus, this statement is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of statement (D)
Complete oxidation of tripalmitin follows the stoichiometry: \(2(\text{C}_{51}\text{H}_{98}\text{O}_6) + 145\text{O}_2 \longrightarrow 102\text{CO}_2 + 98\text{H}_2\text{O}\), giving an \(\text{RQ} = \frac{102}{145} \approx 0.7\). Thus, this statement is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of statement (E)
In living cells, glucose and carbohydrates are the preferred substrates; pure proteins or pure fats are never used alone as isolated respiratory substrates. Thus, this statement is incorrect.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Statements (A), (B), and (D) are correct, while statements (C) and (E) are incorrect. Hence, the correct combination is (A), (B), and (D) only.
